title: Agent evals
summary: Task level evaluation of an agent's end to end behaviour, as opposed to unit tests of its functions.

misconceptions.text: If the unit tests pass, the agent works.

explain: describes evaluation at the level of a whole task, not a single function
names at least one signal that only appears end to end
apply: writes an eval that fails when the agent takes a wrong path
states an acceptance condition before running the agent
discriminate: distinguishes deterministic function checks from task level agent evaluation
gives one example where unit tests pass but the agent fails

title: Unit testing
summary: Checking a single function against expected outputs in isolation.

explain: isolates one unit
states the expected output before running

title: Software testing
summary: Deciding what to check, at which level, and what a failing check tells you.

explain: separates the thing under test from the check
apply: chooses a level of testing that matches the risk

title: Agent loop
summary: The perceive, decide, act, observe cycle that an agent runs until a stop condition.

explain: names the four stages
states one stop condition

title: JSON Schema
summary: Declaring the shape of an object so bad payloads are rejected before they reach the code.

apply: rejects the payload that violates the constraint

title: Feedback loops
summary: Routing the result of an action back into the next decision, and what that does to failure modes.

explain: describes the return path
names one way the loop amplifies an error
apply: closes the loop with a check the agent cannot skip
discriminate: separates a loop that corrects from a loop that amplifies

title: Observability
summary: Being able to answer a new question about a running system without shipping new code.

explain: separates logs, traces and metrics by the question each answers

title: Tool calling
summary: Letting a model select a named function and produce arguments that satisfy its schema.

explain: names the schema as the contract
states who executes the call

title: Cost and latency
summary: Budgeting tokens, calls and wall clock time as first class design constraints.

explain: names one cost driver and one latency driver
states a budget per turn

title: Memory design
summary: Choosing what an agent carries forward, for how long, and what it is allowed to forget.

explain: separates working context from durable memory

title: Threat modeling
summary: Naming who can attack a system, through which surface, and what they gain by it.

explain: names an attacker with a motive
names the surface the attacker reaches
apply: lists one concrete attack path end to end
states the mitigation that closes it

title: Least privilege
summary: Granting the smallest permission that still lets the work happen, and nothing beyond it.

explain: states the permission and the task it exists for
names what is denied by default

title: Prompt injection
summary: Untrusted content reaching a model as if it were instruction from the operator.

explain: separates instruction from data
names one channel the injected text arrives on
apply: blocks the injected instruction without blocking the task

title: Attack surface
summary: Every input, tool and boundary an attacker can reach, counted rather than assumed.

explain: enumerates the reachable inputs
states one way the surface grows
